# chat-demo

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A static chat demo powered by the DeepSeek API. No application backend is required: the browser connects directly to the configured API service.

You can [try the app online](https://deepseek-ai.github.io/chat-demo/) or download the archive from [Releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-chat-demo/releases), extract it, and double-click `index.html` to use it locally without installation or a build. Enter your API key in Settings before your first chat.

## Getting started

Install Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo.git
cd chat-demo
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:8090.

To build the static site:

```sh
pnpm build
```

The output is written to `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web server or open `dist/index.html` directly. Opening the file directly requires browser support for storage on `file://` pages and an API service that permits their cross-origin requests.

## Features

- Multiple conversations with automatic titles, renaming, and deletion; edit prompts, regenerate replies, and switch between message branches.
- Streaming replies, deep thinking, smart search, link reading, and source citations; stop generation or continue eligible replies.
- Upload, paste, or drag and drop attachments; use voice input and read replies aloud. A live audio spectrum appears in the first row of the input area while recording on mobile.
- Markdown, syntax highlighting, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams.
- Simplified Chinese and English, light and dark themes, mobile layouts, location settings, and chat history import and export.

## Data and storage

Your API key and settings are stored in the browser's localStorage. Conversations and original attachments are stored in IndexedDB. Local data is isolated by browser profile and site origin. Sending messages, uploading attachments, and using speech features sends the relevant content to the configured API service.

History import and export in Settings use ZIP archives. After confirmation and successful validation, importing replaces all local conversations and attachments. Exports include conversations and locally available original images, but exclude API keys, settings, and original non-image attachments. See the [history import/export documentation (Chinese)](src/services/chat/history/README.md) for the archive format and preservation details.

Settings → Data → Delete all chats clears all local conversations, original attachments, and unsent drafts after confirmation. It stops ongoing replies and returns to a new chat. Your API key and settings are preserved; files already uploaded to the API service are not deleted.

makepad/relax.content:
# Relax

> [!WARNING]
> **Experimental.** Relax is for development iteration: running, testing and live-editing your program while you work on it. Build anything you release with Rust itself: `cargo build --release` with rustc. So far it has been tested mostly in Makepad's own edit-run loop and only lightly on other projects, so expect rough edges elsewhere and please report them.

### Rust without the wait.

**rustc builds your program, then you run it. Relax runs your program while it builds it.**

Relax is a live compiler and JIT runtime for Rust, written in Rust. It runs a Cargo package straight
from source, with no rustc, LLVM or linker in the loop: it compiles each function when it is first
called, optimises the hot ones while the program runs, and patches your edits into the running process.

## Relax vs cargo and rustc

| | cargo + rustc | **Relax** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Large 3D game, clean checkout → first frame** | ~3 min build, then start | **11 s** on an M4 MacBook, straight from source |
| **Same game, second run → first frame** | start the built binary | **1.15 s** on an M4 MacBook, nothing recompiled |
| **Small app → first frame** | build it first | **3.7 s** cold, **0.41 s** warm (M4 MacBook) |
| **Change one function in a running program** | rebuild, relink, restart: state lost | **patched in**: state kept |
| **Save a file → 92 tests re-run** | rebuild the test binary first | **2.2 s** after the save |
| **Type and borrow check** | `cargo check`; a build checks everything first | `relax check`; a run type-checks each function before it runs and borrow-checks in the background |
| **Speed of optimised code** | 1.00× (`--release`) | **slower: 1.12× the time on x64, 1.24× on arm64** (geomean of 21 workloads) |
| **Needs** | rustc, LLVM, a linker | **one Rust library**: 438k lines, 0 crates.io dependencies |

Code generation for x86-64 and AArch64; from a fresh clone the repository
builds and its tests pass on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64. Windows isn't tested.

## The tradeoffs

- **Slower optimised code.** Overall the code Relax runs is slower than rustc's `--release`: 1.12× the time on x64
  and 1.24× on arm64 (geomean of 21 workloads), 1.22× and 1.25× against a native-CPU build. It is faster on only
  a few workloads: see [where LLVM still wins](#where-llvm-still-wins).
- **More memory.** The compiler, its caches and every code version it publishes share your program's
  process, and JIT code is append-only. `relax inspect <pid> memory` shows the split, `code` the growth.
  The code cache in a package's `target/relax` takes 120 to 190 MB for `hello`.
- **`relax check` isn't faster than `cargo check` yet.** On a large package a cold check takes longer
  and uses more memory than `cargo check`, and an edit can re-check more than it needs to. We're
  working on it.
- **Not every crate runs yet.** [libs/relax/KNOWN_GAPS.md](libs/relax/KNOWN_GAPS.md) lists the open
  gaps, each with a repro.
- **Not every edit patches live.** F…

Run Cloudflare Workers anywhere: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or your own servers.

The same developer experience, without the runtime limits, for a fraction of the bill.

Docs · Deploy · Migrate · Bindings · Examples · Discord

## What is OpenOrange OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. It's built with four goals: - **Zero refactoring, zero-downtime migration**: your Workers and Durable Objects run as they are, and your data moves off Cloudflare while your app keeps serving. - **The same developer experience**: `wrangler dev` becomes `orange dev`, and everything underneath is open source and self-hostable. - **Simpler bills**: you pay for the machines you run on, not Cloudflare's metering or an enterprise contract. Compute is 4.8× cheaper and storage 8.7× cheaper. - **Built for scale**: storage is backed by S3, so scaling out is a matter of adding machines. ## Quickstart You need a Worker project with a `wrangler.jsonc`, `wrangler.json`, or `wrangler.toml` (or use [`examples/hello-durable-object`](examples/hello-durable-object)), Node.js 22 or later, and pnpm. Do not change my app code. ``` ### Step 1: Install Install the `orange` CLI globally, then run it in your Worker project. opencoredev/islandcn.content: # islandcn A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://islandcn.dev/r/island-core.json ``` ```tsx "use client"; import { Island, IslandProvider, useIsland } from "@/lib/island"; // Mount once near the root. ; // Then, from any component inside it: const island = useIsland(); const upload = island.start({ id: "upload", label: "Uploading report.pdf", compact: { leading: , trailing: }, expanded: { center: report.pdf, bottom: }, }); upload.update({ compact: { trailing: } }); upload.end(); ``` ## What's here - **The engine** (`lib/island/`, registry item `island-core`): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only. - **Presets** (`components/islandcn/`): upload, timer, now playing, incoming call, ride or delivery ETA, recording, nearby transfer, battery and the split, each one file on the engine, plus the content kit they share. - **The playground** (`/playground`): build an island for your app from a preset or a blank activity, fire every action, tune the motion and copy the install command and the code. - **The site and docs** (`app/`, `docs/content/`). Coding agents can use the optional `islandcn-skill` registry item as an install helper; see `/docs/agent-skill`. ## Develop ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev # http://localhost:3000 pnpm typecheck pnpm build # builds the registry into public/r, then the site ``` Read `AGENTS.md` before changing anything. # ai-texture-forge

**An AI-powered texture forge for Blender — turn text prompts into seamless PBR materials, concept art and scene-wide projections with local or cloud diffusion models, straight inside the 3D viewport on Windows.**

[download-url]: https://github.com/linknimiball1974/ai-texture-forge/releases

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11-3776AB) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078D6) ![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D) ![Stable Diffusion](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-Stable%20Diffusion-8A2BE2) ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-active-2EA44F)

[![Download](docs/download-button.svg)][download-url]

**The forge in one scene:** type `weathered copper, green patina, seamless` in the N-panel, pick a provider, and a tile-ready PBR set lands on the active object — color, roughness and normal maps wired in one click; one depth-aware projection later, the whole alley is skinned before the coffee cools.

## Why

Texturing from stock libraries is a grind: hours hunting for a texture that only sort of fits, seams stitched by hand in an image editor, round-trips through external AI tools that break your flow, and licenses that never quite cover the project. ai-texture-forge moves generation into the 3D viewport — you describe the surface, the forge renders it with a local GPU engine or a connected cloud provider, bakes seamless tiling, projects it across the scene by depth and wires the maps into Blender's shader nodes — so a project travels from blockout to fully textured render in one sitting without leaving Blender.

## Without / With

| Without | With |
|---|---|
| Hunting stock libraries for a texture that sort of fits | Type the surface you want and generate it on the spot |
| Seams stitched by hand in an image editor | The Seamless option bakes perfect tiling into every generation |
| Round-tripping through external AI tools and re-importing images | Generation runs inside the viewport and lands straight on the object |
| Skinning a whole scene object by object | One depth-aware projection textures the entire scene in a pass |
| Low-res outputs that fall apart in close-ups | AI upscaling lifts generations 4× with the detail intact |

## Quick Start

1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp-for-blender-pro**, then open **3D Viewport → N → MCP Pro**.
4. Choose a provider, add your connection details and select a model.
5. Send a message in Blender or click **Open Studio Window**.

## Features

- **Generate from a text prompt** — textures, concept art and background assets from a plain description, with prompt presets that get the look right on the first try.

# FailSafe ARTEX

A source-built, locally bound distribution of [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX), an open-source multi-agent security testing harness. This repository exists because the prebuilt `tomicdd/artex` Docker image was found to contain an unauthenticated command-execution backdoor in November 2026. This build is compiled from the audited `v0.3.15` source tag and keeps upstream's full runtime capabilities, including Node 22, Playwright, Chromium, and nmap. The compose file binds the console to localhost and does not publish the recording proxy. > **Authorized testing only.** ARTEX runs an autonomous agent that can execute > shell commands and send network traffic. Use it only against systems you own > or have explicit written permission to test. ## Managed ARTEX runs FailSafe can host and run ARTEX safely for you using **GlassBreak**, our cyber-grade model. We handle the isolated runtime, scoping, evidence handling, and the operational controls that are easy to get wrong in a self-hosted deployment. If you want a managed run, contact us: - **Email:** [hello@getfailsafe.com](mailto:hello@getfailsafe.com) - **Contact form:** ## Quick start Requirements: Docker Engine with Compose v2, and about 5 GB of free disk (the browser stack and Chromium account for most of the image size). If you left the LLM key blank, configure a provider in the console before starting a scan.
